Definition: from G5610; belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively)):--beautiful.
BiblicalUsage: hōraîos means beautiful. It occurs 4 times in all, and the passages I have picked — Matthew, Acts, and Romans — show it in its plain sense. I read it as a word that does its work quietly, without dressing anything up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hōraîos matters because beauty in Scripture is never skin-deep — it is the feet that carry good news. I hold that reading it plainly keeps me honest about what God actually said.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
